practice.statementHtml: Read count from 0 to 10, then count numbers from -100 to 100. Print Count and numbers: then one line A N Z per record. Use field-based text output rather than raw structure bytes.

examQuestions.question: Explain internal and trailing structure padding.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Internal padding places later members at suitable aligned offsets. Trailing padding makes the complete structure stride suitable for successive elements in an array. Both contribute to sizeof the structure. Exact gaps depend on the implementation.

examQuestions.question: On a target with one-byte char and four-byte int aligned to four, explain possible Spread and Grouped layouts.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Spread can place char at zero, int at four after three gap bytes, and final char at eight, then end at twelve after trailing padding. Grouped can place int at zero and chars at four and five, then end at eight. These are target-specific layouts, not universal C sizes. Use sizeof, offsetof, and _Alignof to inspect the actual implementation.

First at zero: 1
No overlap: 1
Enough space: 1

The first member starts at zero; later ordinary members do not overlap; the whole object contains its last member.
